newsitem.title: THAILAND: Seagate aims for $19.5 bln revs by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Seagate aims for $19.5 bln revs by 2001.

text.p: Seagate Technologies Inc chairman and chief executive officer Alan Shugart said on Monday his company hopes to report revenues of $19.5 billion by the year 2001.
"My goal for the company for the year 2001 is to have revenues of $19.5 billion," Shugart told Reuters in an interview during a visit to Bangkok.
Seagate had $8.6 billion in revenues in the year ending June 28, 1996. For the first half of the year to December 27, the company reported net sales of $4.46 billion.

Software will be a much bigger portion of the company's revenue by 2001 than it is now, Shugart said. He said it should be about five times larger than the $210 million per year portion it currently represents.
Shugart said Asia represents the fastest growing region for Seagate, the world's largest independent disk drive maker.
"In five to 10 years from now, I think the Asia-Pacific region will be about 30 percent of our revenues," Shugart said. "It's really the fastest growing part of our market."
In the second quarter of the year the region accounted for about 16 percent of Seagate's $2.4 billion revenues, he said.

On the production side, Seagate expects its Thailand operations to expand further in the rest of the century. The company, Thailand's largest private employer, currently employs 37,000 people, but that should expand to 50,000 by the end of the century, Shugart said.
